text:
maria: quick q — ran the TF plan for the per-model flags change and noticed the plan wants to remove a kubernetes_secret and instead put an encrypted value into a ConfigMap. Did we intentionally switch secret wiring for model configs?

ishaan: that was my PR (https://git.internal/redwood/platform/infra/pull/183). intent was to stop creating k8s Secret resources and keep an encrypted blob in the ConfigMap so the secret-controller sync loop doesn't keep touching pods. we decrypt at runtime.

sam: curious — does the plan remove the secret resource entirely or just stop writing it from TF? wondering about leftover secrets in clusters post-apply.

ishaan: TF will taint/delete the kubernetes_secret resource (so it will be removed on apply). the workflow is: create encrypted blob with KMS -> store base64 ciphertext in configmap.data.model_flags -> runtime agent uses instance role to call KMS decrypt. no pod env secretRef.

maria: ok but two concerns: 1) audit/compliance — private/on-prem installs require HSM-backed KMS and clear audit trail, 2) rollout impact — deleting a secret then adding a configmap could trigger different controllers. pinging security but want infra to check the plan. :eyes: 

sam: also saw the plan includes a random_id change that will update a checksum annotation on the deployment and cause rolling restarts. can we avoid that churn for the rollout?

ishaan: good call. I added the random id to force rollouts for old clusters but can make it opt-in. I'll push a follow-up to make checksum rotation conditional on a flag.

maria: can you paste the small terraform diff snippet that does the secret->configmap switch? will attach to the security ticket.

ishaan: paste below — it's the relevant bit:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "model_flags" {
  metadata {
    name = "redwood-model-flags-${var.model_name}"
    annotations = {
      "redwood/config-checksum" = random_id.flags_checksum.hex
    }
  }
  data = {
    model_flags = base64encode(aws_kms_secrets.encrypt["${var.model_name}"].ciphertext)
  }
}

# previous TF had kubernetes_secret.redwood_model_flags which is removed
```

maria: thanks. @sam i'll defer the rollout question to you for the moment — if we gate the checksum rotation behind a terraform var we can keep existing clusters stable.

sam: SGTM. one more infra gotcha — the runtime needs new IAM permission (kms:Decrypt) for instance profile / pod role. plan shows an aws_iam_role_policy_attachment being added. add a note in the PR about least-priv scope (key ARN only).

ishaan: yep I'll scope it. also leaving a migration note in the PR description for ops: run apply in staging, verify pods can decrypt, then prod.

maria: cool. i'll open a security ticket with the PR link and ask for a 24h review window. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: terraform plan summary: -1 kubernetes_secret.redwood_model_flags, +1 kubernetes_config_map.redwood_model_flags, +1 aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ec2_kms_decrypt, 0 other. plan shows 1 to add, 1 to destroy, 1 to change.
